question: The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) of rectangle \(ABCD\) intersect at \(O\). Also, \(AE\perp BD\) at \(E\), and \(\angle DAE=3\angle BAE\). Find the measure of \(\angle EAC\) in degrees.
solution: \(\angle BAE=22.5^\circ\) and \(\angle DAE=67.5^\circ\). In right triangle \(ABE\), \(\angle ABD=67.5^\circ\), so \(\angle ADB=22.5^\circ\). Since \(OA=OD\), \(\angle DAO=22.5^\circ\). Therefore, \(\angle EAC=67.5^\circ-22.5^\circ=45^\circ\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The perpendicular \(AE\) splits the right angle \(DAB\) into angles in the ratio \(1:3\), so \(\angle BAE=90^\circ/4=22.5^\circ\). In right triangle \(ABE\), this gives \(\angle ABD=90^\circ-22.5^\circ=67.5^\circ\).

To find the angle made by \(AC\), compare \(\triangle BAD\) and \(\triangle ABC\). They have \(BA=AB\), \(AD=BC\), and \(\angle BAD=\angle ABC=90^\circ\), so they are congruent by SAS. Corresponding angles give \(\angle BAC=\angle ABD=67.5^\circ\). Both \(AE\) and \(AC\) lie inside the right angle at \(A\), so
\[
\angle EAC=\angle BAC-\angle BAE
=67.5^\circ-22.5^\circ=45^\circ.
\]
solutionMethods.label: Use congruent triangles
